# iPRA derivations of theorems from the proof packets

The [iPRA unification plan](../UNIFICATION-PLAN.md)
sets out how shared arithmetic proofs here are reused at
Foundation symbols and in application endpoints.

This directory holds actual derivations, in intuitionistic primitive recursive
arithmetic, of theorems whose proofs are outlined in the research packets of
[`docs/proofs/`](../docs/proofs/README.md).

The derivations are in the embedded calculus `Prf PRAAx` of
[`ConciseIPRA`](../ConciseIPRA/README.md). This is iPRA in its usual
form: a function symbol for every primitive recursive definition, its defining
equations, the successor axioms, and induction for quantifier-free formulas, over
intuitionistic natural deduction with equality. Closed object-theory endpoints
have the type

```lean
([] : List (Fm PTm 0)) ⊢[PRAAx] φ
```

for an explicit iPRA sentence `φ`, checked by Lean's kernel. The library also
contains externally stated proof-generator and obstruction metatheorems,
identified in the module descriptions and source-claim audit. The transfer
theorem `ConciseIPRA.pra_iff_native` applies to the ordinary object derivations.
The audit file
[`Checks/Axioms.lean`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Checks/Axioms.lean) checks every
declaration of every module of the library (nothing is registered by hand): the
build fails unless each depends only on Lean's standard `propext`, `Quot.sound`
and `Classical.choice` in the metatheory.

The Lake library is `IPRADerivations` (namespace `LeanProofs.IPRA`), built with

```bash
lake build IPRADerivations
```

The [packet progress index](PROGRESS.md) tracks the full source scope and the
newly verified statements.
The [FIBER claim audit](FIBER-CLAIMS.md) maps every claim in that packet to
its exact checked scope and remaining obligations.
The [finite-demand claim audit](FINITE-DEMAND-CLAIMS.md) covers all 17 theorem
environments in that packet and the required scheduling, metric and norm
constructions.
The [Minkowski claim audit](MINKOWSKI-CLAIMS.md) covers its six source theorem
environments, finite-volume appendix and remaining mesh-extractor obligations.
The [Gamma claim audit](GAMMA-CLAIMS.md) retains all 62 source-ledger families
and distinguishes finite factor/tail names from the remaining analytic endpoints.

## Layout

The [Analysis directory guide](Lean/IPRADerivations/Analysis/README.md) lists the topic subdirectories and gives an example import path.

The library is built bottom-up. Reusable layers come first:

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`Core/Basic`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Basic.lean) | Symbols for `+`, `*`, predecessor and truncated subtraction, their defining equations at arbitrary terms, congruence, quantifier-free induction on an open formula (`ind`), and instantiation of closed derivations (`inst`) |
| [`Core/Semiring`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Semiring.lean) | The commutative-semiring laws, additive cancellation and the successor axioms at arbitrary terms, each derived by induction |
| [`Core/Quotient`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Quotient.lean) | Terms modulo provable equality under a context `Γ` form a cancellative commutative semiring `Q Γ` |
| [`Core/Integers`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Integers.lean) | Integers as differences: integer terms `ZT` with their iPRA equation `ZT.eq`, and the ring of differences `Groth (Q Γ)`, in which integer identities are proved by `ring` and `linear_combination` |
| [`Core/Tactic`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Tactic.lean) | Universal closures `allN` and `univ`, and the tactic `ipra_ring` for polynomial identities |
| [`Core/Definitions`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Definitions.lean) | `toPR`, the symbol computing an open term; definitions by primitive recursion from a base and a step term, with their equations; finite sums and products, powers and factorials |
| [`Core/Sums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Sums.lean) | Theorems with the summation bound as an iPRA variable, by induction: Gauss's sum, the sum of odd numbers, telescoping for every unary symbol `f`, and summation by parts (Abel; `von_mangoldt_totient_ipra_2026-11-15` `thm:abel`, in its natural-number form with the index shifted to start at `0`) for all unary symbols `a`, `b` (`Sums.abel_summation`) |
| [`Core/Monus`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Monus.lean) | Truncated subtraction: `0 ∸ b = 0`, `Sa ∸ Sb = a ∸ b`, `(a + b) ∸ b = a`, `a ∸ (a + c) = 0`, zero-or-successor, and the joint induction giving `(a ∸ b) + b = (b ∸ a) + a` and `(a ∸ b)(b ∸ a) = 0` |
| [`Core/Signum`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Signum.lean) | The nonzero indicator `1 ∸ (1 ∸ x)` and its equations at zero and successors. Search and Euclidean arithmetic use this module directly or through their core dependencies. |
| [`Core/Order`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Order.lean) | `a ≤ b` as `a ∸ b = 0` and `a < b` as `S a ≤ b`: witnesses `b = a + d`, reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry, totality, `lt_or_le`, decidability of equality, monotonicity of `+` and `*`, and cancellation |
| [`Core/Pairing`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Pairing.lean) | The equality test `eqb`; the integer square root by primitive recursion, with `isqrt z² ≤ z < (isqrt z + 1)²` and uniqueness; the pairing `⟨a, b⟩ = (a + b)² + a` with projections; simultaneous primitive recursion of two sequences, with both pairs of equations; `h.fstE` and `h.sndE` read off the components of a term that equals a pair (`z ≐ ⟨a, b⟩` gives `fst z ≐ a` and `snd z ≐ b`) |
| [`Core/Powers`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Powers.lean) | `a^{m+k} = aᵐ aᵏ`, `a ≤ b → aᵐ ≤ bᵐ`, `S a ≤ (S a)^{S m}`, and no square strictly between `k²` and `(k + 1)²` |
| [`Core/Parity`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Parity.lean) | `par` and `half` by recursion; `x = 2 half x + par x`, `x` even or odd, `par (2k) = 0`, `par (2k + 1) = 1`, and `2k ≠ 2m + 1` |
| [`Core/BoundedSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/BoundedSums.lean) | Sums of terms as bounded universal quantifiers: a zero sum has zero terms below its bound, and terms that are zero for every index give a zero sum |
| [`Core/Descent`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Descent.lean) | Generic infinite descent: an indicator `χ(a, b)` with a solution bound `a < β(b)` and a step from a solution with `b ≠ 0` to a smaller one is refutable; proved by induction on the count of solutions with `b < N` |
| [`Core/DescentEx`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/DescentEx.lean) | Infinite descent whose step need only prove `∃ a' b'. χ(a', b') = 1 ∧ b' < b`, so a step may branch into cases with different witnesses |
| [`Core/ClockedDescent`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/ClockedDescent.lean) | [`flt_ipra`](../docs/proofs/diophantine-number-theory/flt_ipra/) (`lem:clocked`) | Clocked descent as a schema: for a quantifier-free `P(s)` and terms `D(s)`, `r(s)`, a derivation of `P(s) → P(D(s)) ∧ r(D(s)) < r(s)` yields `∀ s ¬P(s)`. The orbit `D^k(s)` is a primitive recursion; from `P(s)` with `R = r(s)` an induction on `k` gives `P(D^k(s)) ∧ r(D^k(s)) + k ≤ R`, impossible at `k = R + 1`. No infinite sequence or least counterexample is used. |
| [`Core/IntCancel`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/IntCancel.lean) | Cancellation of a nonzero integer factor, `X ≠ 0 → XK = 0 → K = 0`, proved in the object theory (the ring of differences need not be a domain) |
| [`Core/MultiSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/MultiSums.lean) | Bounded sums and products with two parameters: defining equations, congruence below the bound (at different parameters), products of products, delta products `∏_{j<N} F(j)^{[c = j]} = F(c)` and delta sums `∑_{i<N} [i = c] = 1` for `c < N` |
| [`Core/Pigeonhole`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Pigeonhole.lean) | (infrastructure: `dirichlet_kronecker_ipra` `lem:php`, `minkowski_ipra` `lem:php`, `pell_ipra_2026-11-15` `lem:pigeonhole`, `thm:modular`) | The pigeonhole principle with explicit bounded-search witnesses: for `σ(i) < K` (all `i`), `j₀ = μ j ≤ K. ∃ i < j. σ(i) = σ(j)` and `i₀ = μ i < j₀. σ(i) = σ(j₀)` satisfy `i₀ < j₀ ≤ K`, `σ(i₀) = σ(j₀)`; without a repetition every value count is `≤ 1`, contradicting the total `K + 1` (`sum_fiber`) |
| [`Core/Permutation`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Permutation.lean) | Invariance of a bounded product under a permutation with explicit inverse, `∏_{i<N} F(σ(i)) = ∏_{j<N} F(j)`, via the fiber identity `∏_{i<M} F(σ(i)) = ∏_{j<N} F(j)^{m_M(j)}` (by induction on `M`) and `m_N(j) = 1` |
| [`Core/Division`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Division.lean) | Remainder and quotient by recursion on the dividend; for `K ≥ 1`, `z = K quo z + rem z` with `rem z < K`, and uniqueness of quotient and remainder |
| [`Core/Gcd`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Gcd.lean) | Divisibility as `rem x d = 0`, with closure under sums, multiples and differences and cancellation of a positive factor in `≤`; the Euclidean algorithm as a simultaneous recursion, its termination within `b + 1` steps, preservation of common divisors, and the gcd theorem: every common divisor divides `gcd(a, b)`, which divides `a` and `b` when positive (used by `mordell_weil_ipra`, `ipra_categorical_methods`) |
| [`Core/Search`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Search.lean) | Bounded search `μ_{i<N} [f(i, x) = 0]` by primitive recursion, with its specification: a zero below `N` is found, at or before it, and no earlier index is a zero. With the bounded sums and products of `Core/Definitions` and `Core/MultiSums` (a count is the sum of a characteristic function), this is the bounded-fold closure of [`von_mangoldt_totient_ipra_2026-11-15`](../docs/proofs/analytic-number-theory/von_mangoldt_totient_ipra_2026-11-15/) (`lem:bounded-fold`); the search returns the bound when there is no witness |
| [`Core/Evaluation`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Evaluation.lean) | Numeral completeness for closed PR terms. With the Lean-side evaluator `PR.ev` (and `PTm.ev` for terms under a valuation), every symbol applied to numerals is provably the numeral of its value, `app f (num ∘ a) ≐ num (ev f a)` (`eval_app`, by structural recursion on `f`, unrolling `prec` by meta-level induction with `precZero`/`precSucc`); hence `t[num ∘ ρ] ≐ num (ev t ρ)` (`eval_term`), terms of equal value are provably equal (`eval_eq`), and ground terms in any context equal their values (`eval_closed`, `eval_ground`). Kernel evaluation is practical only for small arithmetic; division and gcd codes are too slow to evaluate this way. |
| [`Core/SearchParameters`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SearchParameters.lean) | The same bounded-search proof for an arbitrary finite family of parameters. The result is the least zero below the bound, or the bound when no witness exists. A singleton parameter gives the original `Search.mu` term. |
| [`Core/SumLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumLemmas.lean) | Index shift, additivity, congruence under a bounded hypothesis (with different parameters), and `term ≤ sum`; with `Analysis/PowerSums.sum_le` these are the finite-sum compilation patterns of `expected_value_ipra_2026-11-16` (`prop:sum-compile`) |
| [`Core/SumReflect`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumReflect.lean) | Sum reflection `∑_{i<N} g(i, p) = ∑_{i<N} g(N − 1 − i, p)`, the reflected body reading `⟨N, p⟩` as its parameter (`sum_reflect`) |
| [`Core/Fubini`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Fubini.lean) | Finite Fubini `∑_{i<M} ∑_{j<N} a(i, j) = ∑_{j<N} ∑_{i<M} a(i, j)` (nested sums as bodies reading pair parameters), the weighted delta sum `∑_{j<N} [c = j] G(j) = G(c)` for `c < N`, and `∑ 0 = 0`; the exchange of summation is `cor:finite-fubini` of `expected_value_ipra_2026-11-16` |
| [`Core/SquareLayers`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SquareLayers.lean) | Square sums by L-shaped layers: `∑_{i<M} ∑_{j<M} a(i, j) = ∑_{b<M} (∑_{i<b} a(i, b) + ∑_{j<b} a(b, j) + a(b, b))` for any body `a`, by induction on `M` (the square of side `M + 1` adds a column, a row and a corner) |
| [`Core/BlockSum`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/BlockSum.lean) | Block regrouping `∑_{k<mn} g(k) = ∑_{i<m} ∑_{j<n} g(i n + j)` (`block_sum`, by induction on `m` with `sum_split`), the division identity `⌊(i n + j)/n⌋ = i`, `(i n + j) mod n = j` for `j < n` (`qr_block`), and the flattening form of finite Fubini `∑_{k<mn} a(⌊k/n⌋, k mod n) = ∑_{i<m} ∑_{j<n} a(i, j)` for `n ≥ 1` (`flatten`; `cor:finite-fubini` of `expected_value_ipra_2026-11-16`) |
| [`Core/ProdLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/ProdLemmas.lean) | Bounded products `∏_{i<N} f(i, x)`: congruence below the bound (with different parameters), `∏ 1 = 1`, a constant product is a power, a product of positive factors is positive, and a zero factor below the bound makes the product zero |
| [`Core/SumOrder`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumOrder.lean) | `sum_le_params`: if `f(i, x) ≤ g(i, y)` for `i < N` then `∑_{i<N} f(i, x) ≤ ∑_{i<N} g(i, y)`, with different parameters on the two sides; and `a ≤ b`, `c ≤ d` give `a + c ≤ b + d` |
| [`Core/OrderCertificates`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/OrderCertificates.lean) | Certificates for inequalities, the analogue of `linear_combination` for `≤`. An element of `Groth (Q Γ)` is `Nonneg` when it is the value of a term; sums, products, numerals and natural powers of `Nonneg` elements are `Nonneg`. A derived inequality `h : Γ ⊢ a ≤ b` has the slack `sl h = ι b − ι a`, which is `Nonneg` (`nn_sl`, the value of `b ∸ a`). `le_of_comb`: if `ι b − ι a = z` and `z` is `Nonneg` then `Γ ⊢ a ≤ b`. The tactic `ipra_le z` derives an inequality from a certificate `z`, a combination of slacks with coefficients that are values of terms (products of slacks allowed), by checking `ι b − ι a = z` with `ring`; `ipra_le z with e` checks it with `linear_combination e` so that derived equations can be used (also written in place, as in `with natEq h`), and `ipra_le z using tac` with an arbitrary tactic. No slack term `monus (…) (…)` is written. Transitivity is `ipra_le sl h₁ + sl h₂`; monotonicity of multiplication is `ipra_le sl h₁ * sl h₂ + ι a * sl h₂ + ι c * sl h₁` |
| [`Core/ParityArith`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/ParityArith.lean) | The arithmetic of parities, i.e. of exclusive-or sums: `par (X + 2Y) = par X`; adding an even number does not change the parity; `par (x + y) = par (par x + par y)`; `par (x + x) = 0`; `par (A + B) = 0` gives `par A = par B`; quantities that differ modulo two by an even amount have equal parities; a bounded sum of even terms is even; and `par m = 0`, `par m = 1` give `m = 2 · half m`, `m = 2 · half m + 1`. |
| [`Core/Telescoping`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Telescoping.lean) | Telescoping sums: `∑_{i<N} a(i+1) + a(0) = ∑_{i<N} a(i) + a(N)`; for a signed sequence `p − q` given by its positive and negative parts, `∑_{i<N} (p(i+1) + q(i)) + p(0) + q(N) = ∑_{i<N} (p(i) + q(i+1)) + p(N) + q(0)`; and, when `(p − q)(N) = (p − q)(0)`, the two sums are equal, i.e. the differences around a closed chain sum to zero. |
| [`Core/SumSplit`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumSplit.lean) | Splitting a finite sum at a cut point: `∑_{i<M+K} g(i, x) = ∑_{i<M} g(i, x) + ∑_{i<K} g(M + i, x)`, where the offset body reads its parameter as the pair `⟨M, x⟩`; and the split at two cut points. |
| [`Core/SumPalindrome`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumPalindrome.lean) | Palindromic sums: if `t(N − 1 − k) = t(k)` for `k < N` (a bounded universal hypothesis), then `∑_{k<N} t(k) = 2 ∑_{k<⌊N/2⌋} t(k) + [N odd] · t(⌊N/2⌋)`; the sum is split at `⌊N/2⌋ + [N odd]`, the upper part is mapped onto the lower one by the symmetry and reflected. |
| [`Core/IntOrder`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/IntOrder.lean) | Order on integer terms, `u ≤ v` as `u⁺ + v⁻ ≤ v⁺ + u⁻`, handled through natural-number witnesses (`v = u + D`); `x² = abs(x⁺ − x⁻)²` is a natural number; `S² ≤ T² → S ≤ T` for natural numbers; and, without square roots, the dot-product bound `x₁x₂ + y₁y₂ ≤ ab` and the triangle inequality `(x₁ + x₂)² + (y₁ + y₂)² ≤ (a + b)²` from `x₁² + y₁² ≤ a²`, `x₂² + y₂² ≤ b²`, i.e. `abs(u + v) ≤ abs(u) + abs(v)` for Gaussian integers (the Lagrange identity gives `(ab)² ≥ (x₁x₂ + y₁y₂)²`). Used for the complex estimates of `FTA_iPRA`. |
| [`Core/IntCertificates`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/IntCertificates.lean) | Certificates for inequalities between integer terms, the `zle` analogue of `Core/OrderCertificates`: the slack `zsl h` of a derived `zle u v` is `Nonneg` (`nn_zsl`), and `toZ v − toZ u = z` with `z` `Nonneg` gives `zle u v` (`zle_of_comb`, and `zle_of_comb_two` for certificates of twice the slack, via `le_of_two_mul`); finite sums and squares of integer values are `Nonneg` (`nn_sum`, `nn_zsq`); two-sided product bounds `−AB ≤ ab ≤ AB` (`zabs_mul`); the finite Cauchy inequality `(∑ uᵢ)² ≤ d ∑ uᵢ²` (`cauchy_int`, from `pair_sq`); a `Nonneg` certificate equal to `−1` is contradictory (`false_of_comb`); and the tactics `zsimp`, `znn`, `ipra_zle`. Signed rational estimates cleared of denominators become iPRA derivations this way. |
| [`Core/LinearCombination`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/LinearCombination.lean) | Equations as linear combinations, with the simp set `ipra_defs` of [`Core/CertificateAttr`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CertificateAttr.lean): `ipra_lc e` derives `s ≐ t` or `ZT.eq u v` as the linear combination `e` of ring equations `natEq h`, `ZT.toZ_eq h` written inline, after pushing `Q.mk`, `Groth.ι` and `ZT.toZ` through the term operations and unfolding the definitions tagged `ipra_defs` (`ipra_norm`, `ipra_close`). The module imports only `Core/Tactic`, so that using it adds no names to the scope of a module or of the modules that import it. |
| [`Core/CertificateTactics`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CertificateTactics.lean) | One-line order certificates for integer terms, on top of `Core/LinearCombination` and `Core/IntCertificates`: `ipra_zle z with e` and `ipra_zle2` derive `zle u v` from a `Nonneg` certificate `z` (checked by `znn`) modulo the linear combination `e`; `ipra_absurd z with e` derives any formula from a certificate equal to `−1`; `ipra_cast h` lifts a fact `h : a = b` about natural numbers of the metatheory (a table checked by `decide`) to an equation between integer numerals (`ZT.derive_cast`); `ipra_norm` is extended by the slacks `sl`, `zsl` and by finite sums of integer terms. |
| [`Core/CongruenceTactic`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CongruenceTactic.lean) | Congruence of a term in all its arguments from the template and the list of derived equations alone: `ipra_congr (f (var 0) (var 1) : PTm 2) with [ha, hb]` derives `f a b ≐ f a' b'` from `ha : a ≐ a'`, `hb : b ≐ b'`. `EqPair Γ` packs a derived equation with its sides, so that a vector of derivations determines both substitutions of `Prf.eqCongr` (`eqCongrPairs`); the substitutions are pushed back through the term by `simp` with the `subst_f` lemmas, and `vec6_5`, …, `vec12_11` look up the entries of a vector literal beyond the fifth, for templates with six to twelve variables. |
| [`Core/CommonLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CommonLemmas.lean) | Basic lemmas that many modules used to restate under various names, proved once in the namespace `Common` (the module-local names are now aliases): positivity (`pos_of_succ`, `pos_of_one_le`, `one_le_of_pos`, `succ_pos`, `pos_mul`), order (`add_le_add`, `mul_le_mul`, `succ_le_succ`, `le_of_lt_succ`, `lt_succ_of_le`, `ne_of_lt`, `pred_lt`), cancellation of a positive factor (`mul_cancel_le`, `mul_cancel_eq`, `two_mul_cancel`, `le_of_sq_le`, `lt_of_sq_lt`), truncated subtraction (`monus_le_self`, `monus_of_eq`, `monus_succ_of_le`, `monus_monus_of_le`, `add_eq_zero_left`), congruences (`congrPairT`, `congrEqb`, `congrSg`), the equality test and the signum (`eqb_zero_or_one`, `eqb_le_one`, `eq_of_eqb`, `sg_le_one`, `sg_zero_or_one`, `sg_of_one_le`), powers (`pw_one`, `pw_two`, `pw_double`), numerals and explicit-term positivity (`one_pos`, `two_pos`, `one_le_two`, `one_le_mul`, `one_le_two_mul`), strict differences (`monus_succ_of_lt`, `one_le_monus_of_lt`, `monus_succ_lt`, `le_add_monus`) and `mul_one_right`. |
| [`Core/Reindex`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Reindex.lean) | Substitution into a re-indexed body: `subst_reindex2 σ a b f : Syn.subst σ (Syn.subst ![a, b] f) = inst2 f (Syn.subst σ a) (Syn.subst σ b)` and `subst_reindex3` for bodies with three variables; `subst_inst2`/`subst_inst3` with the left side unfolded, which many proofs carried as a local `have`. |
| [`Core/SubstCommand`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SubstCommand.lean) | The command `ipra_subst f [l₁, …]`: states and proves (by `simp [f, l₁, …]`, or entry by entry when `f` applies a program to a vector of arguments) the simp lemma `subst_f` that pushes a substitution through a defined term, `Syn.subst σ (f a b) = f (Syn.subst σ a) (Syn.subst σ b)`, or `(f a b).subst σ = …` for a formula or an integer term; arguments of type `PTm n`, `ZT n`, `Fm PTm n` are substituted and the others kept, and a constant `c : PTm n` gets `Syn.subst σ c = c`. |
| [`Core/InductionTactic`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/InductionTactic.lean) | The tactic `ipra_ind (hQF) [l₁, …]`: quantifier-free induction on variable `0` (`ind`), leaving the base case and the step with the substitutions `Syn.inst zero` and `repl (succ (var 0))` already pushed through equations, connectives, `+`, `*`, `monus`, `pred`, numerals and variables; the bracket adds the substitution lemmas of the other symbols that occur. `ipra_qfind (hQF) [l₁, …]` does the same for the induction rule `PRA.qfInd`, which derives `∀ φ` in a context `Γ`, and also pushes the substitutions through the shifted parameters. |
| [`Core/Header`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Header.lean) | The command `open_ipra`: the five opens with which a module of the library begins (the root namespaces `LeanProofs.ConciseIPRA` and `LeanProofs.IPRA`, the syntax operations `Syn`, the notation of formulas and derivations, the term constructors `app`, `zero`, `succ`, and `num`, `monus`, `pred`), as one line; module-specific opens follow it |
| [`Core/Bezout`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Bezout.lean) | (with `Core/Gcd` and `Foundations/ChineseRemainder.gcd_pos`: [`mordell_weil_ipra`](../docs/proofs/diophantine-number-theory/mordell_weil_ipra/) `lem:gcd`, and [`faltings_ipra`](../docs/proofs/diophantine-number-theory/faltings_ipra/) `lem:fq-gcd`, Bézout split by sign) The extended Euclidean algorithm with sign-free coefficients and a parity, frozen after termination, and Bézout's identity with natural coefficients: `gcd(a, b) + v b = u a` or `gcd(a, b) + u a = v b` |
| [`Core/EuclidLemma`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/EuclidLemma.lean) | The gcd theorems and Bézout's identity at arbitrary terms; `gcd(a, b) = 0 → a = 0`; `d ∣ x, x ≥ 1 → d ≤ x`; `gcd(p, a) = 1` for a prime `p ∤ a`; Euclid's lemma `prime p → p ∣ ab → p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b` (uses `prime` from `AnalyticNumberTheory/Primes`) |
| [`Core/LinearAlgebra`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/LinearAlgebra.lean) | Integer vectors and matrices: finite sums, dot and cross products, matrix products, traces, determinants by Laplace expansion and adjugates by cofactors, each evaluated to the corresponding Mathlib operation; matrix equations as finite conjunctions |
| [`Core/PolynomialImplications`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/PolynomialImplications.lean) | Implications between integer polynomial equations, `h₁ = h₁' → … → c = c'`: expressions `ZExp k` in `k` integer variables (integer variable `i` is the difference of the natural variables `2i`, `2i + 1`), their value `ZExp.eval` in any commutative ring, the formula `ZExp.imp hyps c`, and `ZExp.derive_imp`: a certificate valid in every commutative ring gives `[] ⊢[PRAAx] univ (2k) (imp hyps c)`. The tactic `ipra_poly R ρ h` opens a certificate, to be closed by `ring` or `linear_combination`. `ZExp.Vec3`, `ZExp.Vec2` with dot, cross and determinants. No cancellation of nonzero factors (the ring of differences is not a domain) |
| [`Core/PolynomialInequalities`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/PolynomialInequalities.lean) | Implications `r₁ → … → r`, each `r` an equation `a = b` or an inequality `a ≤ b` between integer polynomials (`ZExp.Rel`), from a Positivstellensatz-style certificate: it must hold in every commutative ring with a cone (`Cone R`: contains `0`, `1`, sums, products and all squares), `a ≤ b` read as `b − a ∈ C`. `nn_sq`: every square of the ring of differences is the value of a term, so the values of terms form a cone; `ZExp.leF` is the quantifier-free formula of an integer inequality; `ZExp.derive_rel` gives `[] ⊢[PRAAx] univ (2k) (impR hyps c)`. Tactics `ipra_cone R C ρ h` and `cone_mem`; `Cone.of_eq` closes a certificate by `ring` or `linear_combination`. No case distinction on signs (the cone is not total) |

Möbius inversion (`mobius_inversion`) is applied to `f = μ⁻ L_w` and `f = μ⁺ L_w`, whose divisor sums differ by exactly `Λ_w` (`key_inner`: the third form of `thm:lambda-mobius`, extended to `k = 1` via `L_w(1) = Λ_w(1) = 0` as `lambda_mobius_neg'`, after moving the Möbius bound with `mu_bound`); this gives `∑_{d ∣ N} μ(d) Λ_w(N/d) = −μ(N) L_w(N)` (`mu_lambda_conv`, rows by `row_diff`), and `div_swap` gives the stated orientation. |

Equivalently, the tilings of a row of length `n + 1` by squares and dominoes, read as their sets of domino positions, number `F_{n+2}`. `ok(n, b)` is a primitive-recursive scan of the low bits on the state `⟨b ≫ i, flag⟩`, and moving its first step to the front gives `ok(n + 1, b) = [¬(bit₀ ∧ bit₁)] ok(n, ⌊b/2⌋)`. The reusable `∑_{b < 2M} f(b) = ∑_{c < M} (f(2c) + f(2c + 1))` splits by the lowest bit. Since `ok(n + 2, 2c) = ok(n + 1, c)` and `ok(n + 2, 2c + 1) = [c even] ok(n + 1, c)`, this gives `C(n + 2) = C(n + 1) + C(n)`, with `C(0) = 1` and `C(1) = 2`. The cycle: the subsets of the `n`-cycle with no two adjacent elements (also excluding `bit₀ = bit_{n−1} = 1`) number `D(n) = L_n` for `n ≥ 3`. The even `b` contribute `C(n − 1)`. For odd `b = 2c + 1`, with `ok(N + 1, d) = ok(N, d)` for `d < 2^N` (a violation count), the even `c < 2^{n−2}` contribute `C(n − 3)`. Then `F_{n+1} + F_{n−1} = L_n`. |

Some theorems are *schemas*. One Lean theorem then gives an iPRA theorem for
each matrix size `k`, exponent `k` or primitive recursive symbol `f`. Inside each
such iPRA theorem every number variable is a variable of the formula. In the
`Core/Sums` theorems the bound `n` is such a variable, and the derivation uses
the induction axiom of `PRAAx`.

## How the ring tool yields iPRA derivations

Provable equality under `Γ` is a congruence for `+` and `*`, and the semiring
laws are derivable. So the quotient `Q Γ` is a commutative semiring, and
`Q.exact` turns an equality of classes back into a derivation. Integers are
encoded as pairs `(p, q)` standing for `p − q`. The integer equation
`(p, q) = (p', q')` is the quantifier-free formula `p + q' ≐ p' + q`, and
products and sums of pairs are the usual polynomial formulas. Thus an integer
identity such as Heron's formula is a single iPRA equation between explicit
natural-number terms. To derive it, the pairs are evaluated in the ring of
differences of `Q Γ`, where Mathlib's `ring` proves the identity. Cancellation,
derived in iPRA, makes the evaluation injective. Mathlib is used only in the
metatheory, to find and check the derivation. The object-level proof uses only
the axioms `PRAAx`.

For larger identities, such as those of linear algebra, the term operations
(`Mat.det`, `Mat.adj`, `Vec.cross`, …) are shown once to evaluate to Mathlib's
`Matrix.det`, `Matrix.adjugate`, `crossProduct` and so on. An identity is then
proved over an arbitrary commutative ring, for instance by `Matrix.mul_adjugate`,
and read back as an iPRA derivation. This is how a single Lean theorem gives
iPRA theorems for matrices of every size.

## Working patterns for finite sums and signed quantities

Most packet theorems reduce to statements about bounded sums `ap2 (sumF body) N x`, where `body : PTm 2` has the
summation index as variable `0` and one parameter as variable `1`, and `inst2 body i x` is its value. The rules below
are the ones that recur; each is a derived iPRA theorem, not a metatheoretic shortcut.

| Step | Lemma | Module |
|---|---|---|
| Recursion | `sum_zero`, `sum_succ'` | [`Core/Definitions`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Definitions.lean), [`Core/BoundedSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/BoundedSums.lean) |
| Equal summands below the bound, possibly with different parameters | `sum_congr_bounded` | [`Core/SumLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumLemmas.lean) |
| Vanishing summands | `sum_zero_of_bounded` | [`Core/BoundedSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/BoundedSums.lean) |
| Sum of two bodies | `sum_add` (`addBody`), `sum_add2`, `sum_mix` (separate parameters) | [`Core/SumLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumLemmas.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/FactorialLambda`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/FactorialLambda.lean), [`Foundations/SignedSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/SignedSums.lean) |
| A factor that does not depend on the index | `sum_scale`, `sum_const_mul` | [`Probability/Independence`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Probability/Independence.lean), [`Probability/Lotus`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Probability/Lotus.lean) |
| Termwise inequality, a summand below the sum | `sum_le`, `term_le_sum` | [`Analysis/RationalArithmetic/Powers/PowerSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Analysis/RationalArithmetic/Powers/PowerSums.lean), [`Core/SumLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumLemmas.lean) |
| Splitting the range, dropping a vanishing tail | `sum_split`, `sum_ext` | [`Core/SumSplit`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumSplit.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/MobiusBounds`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/MobiusBounds.lean) |
| Selecting one index | `sum_delta` | [`Core/Fubini`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Fubini.lean) |
| Exchanging two sums | `fubini` (bodies `rowB`, `colB`, `oB`, `pB` of a three-variable body) | [`Core/Fubini`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Fubini.lean) |
| Double sums | `dsum`, `dsum_rows`, `dsum_add`, `sum_mul_sum`, `dsum_le`, `dsum_scale` | [`Probability/Independence`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Probability/Independence.lean), [`Probability/SymmetrizedMoments`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Probability/SymmetrizedMoments.lean), [`Foundations/DoubleSumScale`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/DoubleSumScale.lean) |
| Reindexing the multiples of `p`, counting them | `reindex_eq`, `count_multiples` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/SumReindex`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SumReindex.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/Totient`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/Totient.lean) |
| Divisor sums as Dirichlet convolutions | `conv`, `cv_at`, `conv_comm`, `conv_assoc`, `pt_n` (Möbius inversion) | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/DirichletLeibniz`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/DirichletLeibniz.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/DivisorSwapP`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/DivisorSwapP.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/ConvolutionAssoc`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/ConvolutionAssoc.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/MobiusSummatory`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/MobiusSummatory.lean) |
| Bounds by a constant; a sum whose term at `0` vanishes | `sum_le_const`, `sum_le_pos_const`, `sum_le_params` (different parameters) | [`Foundations/AuxiliaryEnvelope`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/AuxiliaryEnvelope.lean), [`Foundations/SumPositive`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/SumPositive.lean), [`Core/SumOrder`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/SumOrder.lean) |
| Reindexing with an inequality | `reindex_le`: `Σ_{m<N} [p ∣ m] h(m/p) ≤ Σ_{k<N} h(k)` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/SumReindex`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SumReindex.lean) |
| Counting lattice points of a row | `ind_eq`, `row_count`: `Σ_{b<N} [(a+1)(b+1) ≤ F] = ⌊F/(a+1)⌋` for `N ≥ ⌊F/(a+1)⌋` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/DivisorHyperbola`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/DivisorHyperbola.lean) |
| Products: two bodies, powers of a constant, one selected index, congruent bodies | `prod_mul`, `prod_pw_of`, `prod_delta`, `prod_congr_mod` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/LcmBridgeExact`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/LcmBridgeExact.lean), [`Foundations/ProductPowers`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/ProductPowers.lean), [`DiophantineNumberTheory/ModularCertificate`](Lean/IPRADerivations/DiophantineNumberTheory/ModularCertificate.lean) |
| Permutations and involutions of the index set | `sum_perm`, `prod_perm`, `pair_count`, `pair_prod` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/Totatives`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/Totatives.lean), [`Core/Permutation`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/Permutation.lean), [`Foundations/InvolutionPairing`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/InvolutionPairing.lean) |

| Divisibility by comparing valuations at every prime (no product is split) | `dvd_of_val_le`, `val_PE`, `pri_dvd`, `cb_dvd` | [`AnalyticNumberTheory/BinomialLcm`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/BinomialLcm.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/PrimorialUpper`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/PrimorialUpper.lean), [`AnalyticNumberTheory/BertrandFactor`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/BertrandFactor.lean) |

The same few techniques carry these rules through a proof:

- **Equations and inequalities by certificate.** An equation between natural terms is derived by
  `ipra_ring`, or by `ipra_lc e` for a linear combination `e` of hypotheses `natEq h`, `ZT.toZ_eq h`
  ([`Core/LinearCombination`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/LinearCombination.lean)). An inequality is derived
  by `ipra_le z`, where `z` is a combination of slacks `sl h` of derived inequalities
  ([`Core/OrderCertificates`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/OrderCertificates.lean)). Integer terms (`ZT`, pairs read as differences) use `ZT.derive`,
  `ZT.toZ_eq` and the order certificates of [`Core/IntCertificates`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/IntCertificates.lean)
  (`ipra_zle z with e`, `ipra_absurd z with e` of
  [`Core/CertificateTactics`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CertificateTactics.lean)). A module tags its own definitions with
  `attribute [local ipra_defs]` and these tactics see through them.
- **Congruence by template.** That a defined term respects derived equations in its arguments is
  `ipra_congr (f (var 0) (var 1) : PTm 2) with [ha, hb]`
  ([`Core/CongruenceTactic`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CongruenceTactic.lean)); `.eqRefl x` stands for an argument that does not change.
- **Basic facts once.** Positivity, cancellation, `monus a b ≤ a`, congruence of pairing and of the equality test
  and similar facts are in the namespace `Common`
  ([`Core/CommonLemmas`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Core/CommonLemmas.lean)); a module-local name for one of them is an `alias`.
- **Algebra over opaque terms.** A ring or order step is stated once for arbitrary terms and then instantiated, as
  `col_alg` in [`AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveInversion`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveInversion.lean) or `one_fold` in
  [`AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveCount`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveCount.lean). The certificate then does not depend on how the simplifier
  rewrites the concrete summands.
- **Pointwise lemma first, binder second.** The summand identity is proved for arbitrary terms in an arbitrary
  context. Under the binder of `sum_congr_bounded` or `sum_scale` it is applied after `simp only [shift_pairT]`;
  a hypothesis `h` of the outer context is carried along as `(shift_pos h).wk` or as `h.shift` followed by
  `simpa [Fm.shift, Syn.shift]`.
- **Strong induction.** iPRA has induction for quantifier-free formulas only, so the hypothesis "for all `i < N`" is
  written as an equation `Σ_{i<N} v(i, x) = 0` for a violation term `v` that vanishes exactly when the claim holds;
  `strong_ind` ([`Foundations/StrongInduction`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/StrongInduction.lean)) concludes `v(N, x) = 0` from a step proved in every context, and
  `sum_zero_elim` recovers the hypothesis at an `i < N`. For a claim `a ≤ b` the term is `a ∸ b`; a side condition on the
  parameter is a 0/1 factor of the term (`vB` in [`AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveWeightBound`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveWeightBound.lean)).
- **Several parameters.** A body has one parameter, so several are packed with `pairT`. Each body gets a syntactic
  lemma for `inst2` and an `_at` lemma at an explicit pair, proved with `fst_pair`, `snd_pair`, `congrFst` and
  `congrSnd`.
- **Signed quantities.** A signed coefficient is a pair of natural bodies, as `μ⁺`, `μ⁻` in
  [`AnalyticNumberTheory/Mobius`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/Mobius.lean); a statement `A = B` becomes `A⁺ + B⁻ = B⁺ + A⁻`. For bounded sums of
  signed bodies, [`Foundations/SignedSums`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/SignedSums.lean) gives the rules as ring equations between evaluations
  (`ZB.toZ_sum_congr`, `toZ_sum_add`, `sum_zle`, `ZB3.toZ_fubini`).
- **Rational statements.** Denominators are cleared, so `|C − X/(q l)| ≤ 1` is the pair `q l C ≤ X + q l`,
  `X ≤ q l C + q l` ([`AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveCount`](Lean/IPRADerivations/AnalyticNumberTheory/SieveCount.lean)).
- **Bounded search and decidable conditions.** A bounded existential is a primitive recursive bit with its witness
  (`exB`, `wit`, `ex_cases`, `ex_elim`, `ex_least`, `ex_none` in [`Foundations/BoundedReflection`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/BoundedReflection.lean)), and a
  bounded formula compiles to a bit with a closed correctness proof (`BFm`, `bitF`, `boolean_reflection_closed` in
  [`Foundations/BoundedSyntax`](Lean/IPRADerivations/Foundations/BoundedSyntax.lean)). A decidable side condition can also be multiplied in as a 0/1 factor
  (`eqb s t`, `sg d`), so that a summand identity holds at every index.

## Relation to other iPRA work in the repository

`Computability/DiophantineConsistency` and `Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/PA`
develop iPRA in Foundation's first-order framework (`LO.FirstOrder`, with
`𝗜𝗻𝘁¹` and the language `DiophantineConsistency.PRALanguage`). They target the
consistency equation and Busy Beaver statements. The
[Foundation–ConciseIPRA bridge](../Bridge/README.md) transports closed
derivations between that standard iPRA theory and `Prf PRAAx []`. The
`HA*Arithmetic` modules of `DiophantineConsistency` derive semiring laws in
`SetTheory.PA`. The packets of `docs/proofs/` target `Prf PRAAx` and
`pra_iff_native`, so this library builds its arithmetic layer there.
